transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-01
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (CTO, Sierra), Lena Ortiz (Head of Platform), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Samira Khan (Security)
Shared: Pricing spreadsheet (will be shared), security-pack.pdf, sample-benchmarks.xlsx

Summary (auto): Quick integration discovery to validate patterns for using Redwood hosted vs dedicated for Sierra Payments' chat and automated reconciliation workflows. Focus: SDK support, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy constraints, rate-limiting, and observability hooks for production logging and tracing.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and I'll hand off to Ethan and Carlos to dig into the technical bits. Quick confirm on attendees?
00:12 Ravi: Hi, this is Ravi, CTO. Lena, Marco and Samira here. Good to meet you.
00:18 Maya: Great. Ethan?
00:20 Ethan: Yeah hi, Ethan Chen, solutions engineering. We'll run through how teams typically integrate, SDKs, and then answer questions about gateway / outbound proxy and quotas.
00:30 Lena: We're primarily interested in the integration story - our stack is Node backend services, some Python infra for ML pipelines, and we use LangChain for orchestration in a few prototypes.
00:45 Marco: Also we use Llamaindex for our search vector pipelines, hoping to plug Redwood in without rewriting a lot.
01:02 Ethan: Cool; that's common. Redwood provides first-party SDKs for Python and Node, plus HTTP REST endpoints. Our SDKs include a LangChain connector (and we have a maintained LlamaIndex adapter) - we'll share examples. The SDK supports streaming, tool calls, and embeddings.
01:20 Marco: When you say "LangChain connector", is that an official chain or a wrapper? We've seen community wrappers that get out of date.
01:30 Ethan: It's an official adapter maintained by Redwood's DX team. For LangChain we expose an agent/LLM wrapper that maps Redwood streaming and function-calling into LangChain's interfaces. We publish it on GitHub and version it with SDK releases. There are a few notes in the README about concurrency and tokenization differences.
01:48 Carlos: Quick add - LlamaIndex adapter is available but sometimes pragma differences require small shims in the index build step; we can provide a sample migration script.
02:10 Ravi: Good. On the infra side, we have an outbound proxy and strict egress rules. How does Redwood handle IP allowlisting or in a private deployment - do we need to open dynamic ranges?
02:25 Ethan: For hosted, we publish a list of egress IP ranges and also offer a webhook/callback retry approach. For Dedicated you get dedicated pool and static egress IPs, and for Private (VPC) you can run the control plane on your network. If proxy is required, the SDK honors HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY env vars, but for mTLS or strict network policies, Dedicated or Private is better.
02:48 Samira: For security, we need KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and SOC 2 details. Do you support HSM/KMS?
03:00 Maya: Yes - Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, or on-prem HSM via connectors). We also ship audit logs with per-token request IDs and per-route traces. We'll attach the security pack.
03:18 Marco: Great. A specific question on rate limits - can we do per-customer quotas? Our tenants vary a lot.
03:28 Ethan: Yes, our control plane supports per-API-key rate limits, per-route quotas, and token-based quotas. In Hosted you can do API-key level limits and we can set soft quotas. For Dedicated we can add per-tenant routing policies and stricter reserved capacity. Also concurrency limits can be configured at the route layer.
03:52 Lena: Do you expose those limits in the SDK or via headers so our gateway can react? We prefer graceful 429 handling and backoff.
04:04 Ethan: We return standard 429 with a Retry-After header; SDKs expose exception types and streaming partial results when applicable. We also surface rate-limit metrics to the Console and via observability hooks (webhooks, Prometheus, Datadog).
04:22 Ravi: Observability: we need per-request traces tied to our trace IDs. Is there passthrough for correlation headers?
04:30 Ethan: Absolutely - we recommend passing a x-redwood-trace-id or your trace-id header; Redwood will include it in logs and spans. We provide an OpenTelemetry integration to forward spans into customer backends, and the Console has trace drilldowns.
04:50 Marco: There's often a mismatch in token counting between providers; do you provide per-token count breakdown and per-token cost?
04:58 Carlos: Yes. The Console and API return token usage per request, with model and input/output token counts. Redwood's billing can be broken down per-route. We'll send an example billing export schema.
05:15 Marco: On the SDK level, do you handle KV cache / prefix caching automatically or is that an app-side concern? Our workloads use a lot of repeated prompts.
05:27 Ethan: Redwood supports prefix caching on the runtime side, automatic KV cache for decoder state (to speed up generation), and we have a caching layer for embedding reuse. Some caching (e.g., application-level prompt prefixing) still lives in your app; we can recommend patterns.
05:42 Lena: How invasive is switching to Dedicated? We may want to start hosted and then move. Any pitfalls?
05:52 Maya: Many customers start hosted to validate product/latency, then move to Dedicated for predictable SLOs. The API surface is the same; model versions and keys can be pinned. Main differences are networking, static egress IPs, and reserved capacity provisioning lead time (~2-6 weeks depending on region).
06:12 Ravi: About latency - our SLAs for reconciliation bots are 200-300ms tail for small prompts. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?
06:22 Ethan: For small prompts we have verified p50/p95 numbers for curated models. Hosted can hit 100-200ms p50 in low-latency regions, but p95 depends on load. Dedicated provides more predictable p95. We can run benchmarks with your traffic.
06:40 Marco: We use langchain async patterns heavily. Does the Node SDK support async streaming?
06:48 Ethan: Yes - Node SDK has streamable async iterators and the Python SDK exposes async generators. We also support function/tool calling - mapping to LangChain actions.
06:58 Samira: If we run a POC, and you need to ingest customer PII for test, how is that handled? Retention?
07:08 Maya: Redwood hosted can do no-retention configs and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options. For Dedicated/Private, data residency and retention are controlled by customer configs. We'll include the retention policy matrix in the security pack.
07:28 Lena: On proxying: we can't directly allow wide egress. If we use a gateway that proxies calls and adds auth, any pitfalls?
07:38 Ethan: Fine - common pattern is an internal gateway that holds customer tokens and does request batching. One caveat: streaming responses require a websocket or server-sent events path that your gateway must forward. If your gateway buffers, it can add latency.
07:59 Marco: Good to know. For LlamaIndex ingestion we have embed calls that are batched - what about rate limits on embeddings?
08:08 Carlos: Embeddings are rate and token limited like other routes. We can offer burst capacity in Dedicated, and we also recommend client-side batching. We'll tune the POC for your embed pattern.
08:22 Ravi: About costs: can you provide a TCO example of hosted vs dedicated for 200M tokens/month and 50M embedding units?
08:31 Maya: Yes - I'll send a TCO sheet. Generally, dedicated is better past a threshold (varies by model and quantization). We'll include quantized model options to lower unit costs.
08:44 Samira: Observability hooks - we need log streaming to our S3 and syslog. Is that supported?
08:52 Ethan: Yes; we can stream logs and audit events to S3, or forward them to your SIEM. We also support webhooks for important events (errors, quota hits). For metrics, we push a Prometheus remote write or Datadog.
09:06 Lena: Do you support per-route rollout policies (canary, A/B)? Our platform team needs to slowly roll model changes.
09:15 Carlos: Yes - Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback to previous model variants on regressions. You can declare routes and weights via the API.
09:28 Marco: One more on the integration with our LLM orchestration - does Redwood support function-calling and structured output parsing? We use functions heavily.
09:36 Ethan: Yes - function-calling and structured outputs are supported. We provide typed response parsing helpers in SDKs and examples integrating with LangChain function agents.
09:45 Ravi: Great. Let's talk POC timeline - we want a 2-week POC: setup, ingest sample data, run traffic, and then a benchmark report. Is that realistic?
09:55 Maya: Yes, typical POC is 2-4 weeks. For a tight two-week cycle, we'll need your sample traces and a POC owner on Sierra side.
10:05 Marco: We'll assign that.
10:10 Samira: A compliance question: do you provide field-level encryption for sensitive fields before sending to Redwood?
10:18 Ethan: You can encrypt payloads client-side; Redwood will treat them as opaque tokens. For structured fields we recommend tokenization/PII redaction pre-infer. For deeper use, Private deployments allow you to manage keys and decryption inside your network.
10:34 Carlos: Also worth noting - runtime supports per-route transformations if you want to scrub fields server side before forwarding to model.
10:44 Lena: Nicely flexible. Any SDK version constraints? We run Node 18 and Python 3.10.
10:52 Ethan: Supported - Node 16+ but we recommend Node 18+, Python 3.9+. We'll include compatible SDK version pins.
11:02 Ravi: Are there webhook retry guarantees? We saw missed callbacks before with another vendor.
11:10 Carlos: We support at-least-once delivery with exponential backoff and DLQ to S3 if webhook repeatedly fails.
11:20 Marco: For model selection - do you have a catalog with perf profiles? We need to pick models for latency vs quality tradeoffs.
11:28 Ethan: Yes - our model catalog shows p50/p95 token latencies per region and recommended uses (chat, embeddings, reranking). We'll share the performance profiles spreadsheet.
11:40 Samira: Quick nit: do you do mutual TLS between Redwood and customer endpoints for webhooks?
11:48 Ethan: Yes, mTLS is supported for webhook endpoints on Dedicated/Private; hosted supports IP allowlisting and HMAC signatures for verification.
12:00 Lena: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex node integration? We had issues with tokenizers mismatching.
12:10 Carlos: Tokenizer mismatch can happen if LlamaIndex uses a different BPE. We recommend normalizing tokenization using our SDK's token counters, and we have a small helper to re-tokenize during index build.
12:24 Marco: Perfect.
12:30 Ethan: Should we quickly demo a sample code snippet? I can paste the LangChain adapter usage real quick.
12:35 Maya: Sure - that'll be helpful.
12:38 Ethan: (shares code link) - for Node: const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY}); const llm = new RedwoodLLM({client, model: 'redwood-medium'}); const chain = new LLMChain({llm, prompt}); In LangChain you can use RedwoodLLM as any LLM and stream with llm.stream() - small note: enable keepAlive in your proxy to avoid chunk drop.
13:05 Marco: Nice, that looks straightforward. We'll test the adapter.
13:12 Ravi: Back to quotas - if a tenant exceeds their quota, can we route them to a lower-cost model automatically?
13:21 Carlos: Yes - routing policies can downgrade to a cheaper model variant or route to a fallback endpoint. You can configure thresholds and automatic fallbacks.
13:34 Lena: Anything around cost-optimized quantized models accessible via hosted?
13:40 Ethan: We have quantized variants in the catalog; some are hosted with verified perf profiles. For heavy usage Dedicated can load optimized kernels for quantized models to improve unit economics.
13:52 Marco: How about usage analytics? We want per-tenant, per-route token breakdown with monthly exports.
14:00 Carlos: Console has per-API-key and per-route exports; scheduled reports can be delivered to your S3 or via their API.
14:10 Ravi: Ok, last set: when we run the POC, will you instrument network egress and per-request latency so we can reproduce p95 numbers?
14:20 Ethan: Yes - we'll run a joint benchmark harness that replays your traces, measure p50/p95 and provide the exported results plus trace-level logs.
14:32 Samira: For security review, we'll need the SOC2 report and penetration test cadence.
14:38 Maya: We'll attach SOC2, recent pen test summary, and compliance pack in the follow-up.
14:45 Lena: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
14:50 Maya: Just to recap next steps - I'll send pricing/TCO, Ethan will share code examples and adapters, and we should schedule the POC kickoff.
15:05 Ravi: Sounds good. We'll pick internal POC owner and share workload traces.
15:10 Maya: Awesome - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs + calendar invite.
